rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store. Any file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build.
rules.evidence: Exactly one storage driver import each, both inside the boundary: app/lib/spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10 (package:sqlite3) and app/lib/spine/store/store_web.dart:4 (package:idb_shim). I counted every package: import in app/lib (grep -rhoE 'package:[a-z0-9_]+' | sort | uniq -c): sqlite3 1, idb_shim 1, web 1, path_provider 3, and nothing else that persists. app/lib/spine/store/open_store.dart:8-11 is the only conditional-import fan-out and it is inside spine/. app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:22-37 walks lib/ and fails on any driver import outside lib/spine/; :39-49 additionally confines sqlite3/idb_shim to lib/spine/store/. I re-implemented its regex (persistence_boundary_test.dart:15-19) in Python and probed it with 13 directive shapes: plain single-quoted, double-quoted, export, conditional (`import 'stub.dart' if (dart.library.io) 'package:sqlite3/sqlite3.dart';`), deferred, broken over three lines, `as` alias, bare `package:hive` with no slash, dart:html and dart:indexed_db - it caught all of them. The two it does not catch are `package:web/web.dart` and `dart:js_interop`, which is the hole recorded as a minor finding; the only file outside spine/ that imports them (app/lib/media/local_uri_web.dart:1,4) mints Blob object URLs (:12-14) and touches no storage. Writes outside spine/ are two temp-file media caches (app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:23-29, app/lib/media/read_bytes_io.dart:8-19) derived from blobs already in the log, not a second store of truth. Device-local settings (pairing key, draft, notification prefs, push words) go through Spine.setMeta (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:409-410) into the same store's meta table, i.e. inside the boundary.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, with docs/EVENT_TYPES.md and the code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list.
rules.evidence: Eighteen types in app/lib/spine/types.dart:125-342 and eighteen rows in docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:33-50, in the same order. Every entry carries renderer, notify and search: I checked all 18 have a renderer id present in kThreadRenderers (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:165-180, thirteen own bodies plus `for (final m in kModules) ...m.bodies` at :179), a Notify value consumed by NotificationPrefs (app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:43-47, 76, 115-116), and a SearchSpec consumed by the index (app/lib/spine/search.dart:58, 69-78). Tests: app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18 parses the doc table and asserts documented == registered and length >= 14; app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30 asserts renderer existence in both directions; app/test/floors_test.dart:104-122 asserts every type has a renderer, a Notify and a non-empty-or-excluded search spec. WHY PARTIAL: the doc/code test compares the type-id column only, so the three columns this rule names are unchecked, and two of them are wrong. docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:37 (reaction) promises search 'by feeling, by family' and :41 (feeling) promises 'by feeling, by family, by intensity'; the strings 'family' and 'intensity' do not occur anywhere in app/lib/spine/search.dart or app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart (grep returns nothing), and SearchIndex._index (search.dart:56-84) indexes only textFields, the type id, the facet names and feeling_id. docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:36 similarly promises voice_note search 'media facet, duration' where types.dart:170 declares facets only. Also app/test/floors_test.dart:119 says 'the eighteen the registry holds are all of them present' above a hand-written list of seventeen - passed_on is absent from it and from the identical list at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:21-25.

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line. Check the registry and check that the commit which added the fourth module touched nothing under the first three.
rules.evidence: app/lib/modules/registry.dart:10-16 is the whole registration: five const constructors, one line each. The five directories are app/lib/modules/{dates,todos,calendar,rituals,shelf}/, two or three files apiece and nothing outside them. app/test/module_costs_test.dart:35-75 proves the claim by reading source: for every module it forbids the module id, each of its event type ids and each of the renderer ids the registry names for those types from appearing in quotes in any file under lib/ or web/ except the module's own directory and lib/spine/types.dart - and it walks web/*.js as well as lib/*.dart (:28-33), which is how the service worker's old per-type table was caught. It passes. I confirmed independently: grepping lib/ and web/ for the five module ids and the five event type ids outside lib/modules/ and lib/spine/types.dart returns nothing but MomentsView.milestones (app/lib/regions/moments/moments_region.dart:26, an enum name, not a quoted type id) and lens comparisons that read the registry field (:153). Us shares the desk from kModules and Module.share/rowHeight rather than a table of ids (app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:84-93); search facets come from the registry (app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart:55-62); paper comes from Module.stocks (app/lib/material/assignment.dart:34-41); the thread body table and the away-from-thread sentence come from Module.bodies and Module.sentence (renderers.dart:179, :223-226). HISTORY: the first four modules all arrived in one commit (git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H per directory: dates, todos, calendar and rituals are all d2be5a3d79df2f78c8d36d4059f59403712e6a3c), so there is no separate fourth-module commit; the fifth, shelf, is ffc5821dc89a98dd212ec082791c7ff6d857510c, and its 17-file diff touched nothing under any of the first four directories - one line in registry.dart, its own 180-line module file, spine/types.dart, docs/EVENT_TYPES.md, the seed and validator, plus the then-shared regions/chat/renderers.dart, which no longer exists as a per-module file. Residual cost today is honestly declared at app/lib/modules/module.dart:12-16. I read the diff by path with --format= and did not read any commit message.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events. They must not reach the log.
rules.evidence: Ephemeral is a separate wire type with no path into the store: app/lib/transport/transport.dart:131-147, and PullResponse.ephemeral is documented 'Never stored' at :127. Structurally they cannot become events even by mistake - Spine.append calls specOf(type) (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:219-221) which throws ArgumentError on any id not in kEventTypeById (app/lib/spine/types.dart:346-350), and neither 'typing' nor 'presence' is a registry id; the same guard is applied to events arriving off the wire at spine.dart:274, 284. The send side is a distinct call: app/lib/scope.dart:176 sends Ephemeral(kind: 'typing'), :155-160 expires it on a 6-second timer, and the composer only touches that path (app/lib/regions/chat/chat_region.dart:681-687). app/test/transport_local_test.dart:287-302 sends a typing frame client-to-host and a presence frame host-to-client, asserts both were delivered, then asserts r.host.length == 0 and r.client.length == 0. app/test/reliability_test.dart:117-130 repeats it as a reported capability, comparing host.length + client.length before and after.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread.
rules.evidence: A read marker never becomes a row object at all, so nothing downstream can draw one: app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:278-284 handles 'read_marker' by advancing _readUpto and returning before _add, and :286 returns for any type whose registry entry says rowInThread == false. The registry says so at app/lib/spine/types.dart:225 (read_marker) and :190 (reaction). Belt and braces at the draw site: renderer 'ink_dries' maps to _neverARow, a SizedBox.shrink (app/lib/thread/renderers.dart:174, :139). Marginality is asked of the registry rather than of a second list (app/lib/regions/chat/chat_region.dart:576-582 keys on the renderer id; app/test/thread_types_test.dart:90-110). Tested three ways: spine_schema_test.dart:31-34, thread_types_test.dart:112-120, and app/test/spine_replay_golden_test.dart's 'a read marker moves a mark and is never a row' (green in my run). The capture record names read markers only under 'folded_in' - a count of rows whose delivery is read (chat_region.dart:413-416) - never under 'kinds'.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file. Check history as well as the working tree.
rules.evidence: Working tree: git grep -I -iE 'tskey-[a-zA-Z0-9]|TS_AUTHKEY|BEGIN [A-Z ]*PRIVATE KEY|-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE|authkey' over all 1,614 tracked files returns only the variable name in prose and scripts and the literal placeholder 'tskey-auth-...' with a Unicode ellipsis at tools/tailscale/up.sh:4, :60 and docs/PHONES.md:69. No tracked filename matches key/secret/cert/pem/env/token/auth except unrelated words (git ls-files | grep -iE). tools/tailscale/up.sh:48-51 and bootstrap.sh:217-221 read TS_AUTHKEY from the environment and write only the word 'present' or 'pending' to toolchain/ts/AUTHKEY_STATUS, which .gitignore:15 excludes along with .env and *.authkey (.gitignore:12-14). History: I ran git grep -I -E 'tskey-(auth|api|client)-[A-Za-z0-9]{6,}|-----BEGIN ([A-Z]+ )?PRIVATE KEY-----|-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----|nodekey:[a-f0-9]{16,}|privkey:[a-f0-9]{16,}' across all 321 commits (git rev-list --all). The only hits are two `nodekey:` values in evidence/coldstart.json - Tailscale's public node keys, the same two that stand in the working tree at evidence/coldstart.json:7 and :17, published to the coordination server by design and not an auth key, a private key or a pairing secret. The pairing secret is never written down at all: it is derived by HKDF from the six spoken words and only the derived key is stored (app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:173-174 via Spine.setMeta, cleared at :381-382). NOTE ON HYGIENE: that history grep returned a hit inside a prior cycle's critic report, which the task told me to leave closed. I did not open the file and I have not used anything it said; every claim in this row is from a scan I ran myself.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key.
rules.evidence: BINDING - PASS. isTailnetAddress (app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:22-33) admits only 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48; addressToServeOn (:56-72) refuses a declared address that is not one of those and, with nothing declared, enumerates interfaces and throws NotOnTheTailnet rather than falling back. TailscaleBinding.hostBind (app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:72-79) calls it first, before anything else, so there is no path to 0.0.0.0 - I grepped the transport tree for InternetAddress and wildcard literals and there is none. clientBase (:82-96) refuses to talk to an off-tailnet host. app/test/tailnet_test.dart:11-30 covers 15 addresses including the two just outside the CGNAT range, :32-43 covers four bad declared addresses, :45-62 covers the no-tailnet case. AUTH - PARTIAL. Every /v1 request is checked: app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:100-104 returns 401 before dispatch, and _authenticated (:130-141) requires a stored pairing and key, the right client device id, a timestamp within kAuthSkew, a constant-time MAC over method+path+query+ts+nonce+body, and a nonce not seen before. Pairing itself is 403 outside an open window with a proof check (:150-176). BUT server_io.dart:91-93 sends every path that does not start with kApiPrefix ('/v1', wire.dart:9) to _serveStatic (:304-329), which serves any file under pwaRoot with no authentication at all and falls back to index.html; no test covers it. That is how the iPhone fetches the PWA before a pairing exists, so it is defensible, but it is an unauthenticated surface the rule's wording does not carve out. Two further gaps: in userspace mode boundTo is 127.0.0.1 (tailscale_transport.dart:77) - narrower than the tailnet address, and the evidence says so plainly (evidence/coldstart.json host_listener '127.0.0.1:8443', host_reachable_at '100.68.254.25') - but no test exercises that branch; and the live tailnet check is the one test the suite skipped in this environment ('the tailnet nodes were not answering; the dated run above stands and this check is pending'), so the binding is proven by unit test and by a dated earlier record, not by a run today.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font was downloaded from the internet.
rules.evidence: I walked assets/ myself in Python: 744 files excluding MANIFEST.json, 742 entries, zero entries pointing at a file that is not there, and zero entries with a blank or missing generator field. The two files without an entry are assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json and assets/tears/relief.json, both in the exemption set the checker declares in source with its reason - 'the manifest itself, and the small index files the generators write beside their output' - at tools/check/manifest.py:21-23, alongside MANIFEST.fonts.json, tears.json and INDEX.json. They are records, not library material. Ten distinct generators are named across the 742 entries and all ten exist on disk: blender/{bits/bits.py,folds/fold.py,objects/objects.py,paper/stocks.py,paper/tear_relief.py,shell/desk.py} and tools/{handwriting/build.py,ink_plate.py,sound/synth.py,tears/tear.py}. NOTHING DOWNLOADED: grep -rnE 'urllib|requests\.|urlopen|wget|curl |http://|https://' over tools/ and blender/ .py and .sh finds no fetch in any generator - the only matches are the word 'curl' as a geometry variable, an apt prerequisite list, and the push self-test's example URL. The three fonts are built from tools/handwriting/skeletons.json (a stroke-skeleton table: keys glyphs, metrics, parts, point_format) plus hands.json by tools/handwriting/build.py, whose docstring at :13 states 'Nothing is downloaded'; app/pubspec.yaml has no google_fonts or any font package, and app/test/nothing_is_set_in_an_icon_font_test.dart:16, :21-24 forbids Icons/CupertinoIcons/IconData/IconButton/Icon( and emoji codepoints in every displayed string in lib/. Cosmetic wrinkle, not a failure: evidence/logs/manifest.json reports entries_without_a_file ['fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json', 'tears/tears.json'] and still ok: true, because tools/check/manifest.py:53 removes exempt names from on_disk (:51-55) but :49 leaves their entries in `have`, so the checker lists two of its own exemptions as stale.

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to.
rules.evidence: THEY PASS. I copied app/, docs/, seed/, assets/objects, tools/capture and evidence/scenes to /tmp/lt and ran `flutter test --no-pub` there so nothing in the repository moved: 160 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed, exit 0 (Flutter 3.47.2 from toolchain/flutter). The skip is coldstart_test's live tailnet check, which reports itself rather than passing silently. capture.sh:75-81 is the only place that runs the suite; run.sh and bootstrap.sh do not, and there is no CI, which the script's own comment says. THEY MOSTLY TEST WHAT THEY CLAIM. Several are unusually strong for this kind of guard: module_costs_test.dart:35-75 and persistence_boundary_test.dart:22-49 read source rather than call code, every_module_is_on_the_desk_test.dart:120-199 asks each module's own RenderFitRows how many rows it kept rather than measuring the harness, and every_screen_builds_test.dart:48-58 asserts tester.takeException() is null so the cases that look assertion-free are not. Five that do not: (a) thread_types_test.dart:65 and :86 guard against a stored key reaching a person with expect(line, isNot(contains('_'))), fed by _plausible at :123-139 whose 'feeling_id' => 'hold' (:131) is the one value shape that cannot trip it - it misses a live defect in 390 of the seeded year's 1,340 feeling/reaction events; (b) one_kind_of_paper_per_kind_of_event_test.dart:17-23 hard-codes a five-entry map of module files and all three tests (:26, :40, :50) iterate it rather than kModules, while module_costs_test walks only lib/ and web/, so a sixth module silently loses the check and even the five are scanned one file apiece - the four thread_row.dart files and dates_module.dart are never read; (c) the_record_names_every_kind_test.dart:15-34 is named 'every event type is somewhere a region says it is showing' but compares the registry against four hand-written sets in the test file and asks no region anything; (d) with_the_year_in_it_test.dart:121-125 'the pulse and the modules have something to say' asserts only that two regions build without throwing, while its siblings at :105-111 and :113-119 assert content; (e) with_the_year_in_it_test.dart:83 returns silently instead of markTestSkipped when the bundle has no seeded year, so that case reports green on an unseeded build. I scanned all 54 test files programmatically for cases with no expect/expectLater/fail in the body: five, and four of them delegate to a helper that does assert.

findings.where: summaryOf, the 'feeling' and 'reaction' arms at lines 200-203
findings.what: The one sentence an event reads as away from the thread interpolates the raw feeling_id, so a search result and the reply strip read 'noor sent warm_palm' and 'teo put miss_you on it'; 390 of the 1,340 feeling and reaction events in seed/year carry an underscored id (warm_palm 81, did_it 70, miss_you 62, thinking_of_you 55, long_day 49 and six more), and SearchIndex tokenizes on non-alphanumerics (app/lib/spine/search.dart:18), so searching 'warm' returns exactly those rows.
findings.why: Row 04 is coherence: the same event is a drawn object with a written caption in the thread (renderers.dart:107-127, which uses c.registry.byId and the feeling's human name) and a stored database key in search (search_page.dart:372, 377) and on the composer's replying-to strip (chat_region.dart:976) - the file's own comment at :182-185 and docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:82-86 say this exact failure, a person shown a stored field, is what one sentence per event exists to prevent.

findings.where: the registry table, the search column of rows 5 and 9 (lines 37 and 41)
findings.what: The document promises reaction is searchable 'by feeling, by family' and feeling 'by feeling, by family, by intensity'; neither 'family' nor 'intensity' occurs anywhere in app/lib/spine/search.dart or app/lib/regions/chat/search_page.dart, and SearchIndex._index (search.dart:56-84) indexes only the declared textFields, the type id, the facet names and feeling_id.
findings.why: Rule 2 requires the document and the code to agree on each type's search behaviour, and the only test that compares them (app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:10-15) parses the type-id column alone, so the other three columns of the table are asserted by nothing and two of them have drifted.

findings.where: the underscore guards at lines 65 and 86, and the fixture at line 131
findings.what: The guard that no type shows a person a stored key is fed 'feeling_id' => 'hold', a value with no underscore in it, so the assertion expect(line, isNot(contains('_'))) cannot fail for the two types whose sentences interpolate that field.
findings.why: Rule 9: the test asserts something weaker than its name, and the thing it was written to catch is live in the product (finding 1) with the suite green.

findings.where: the _moduleTypes map at lines 17-23, read by all three tests at :26, :40 and :50
findings.what: The check that no module names its own paper reads a hard-coded map of five module ids to five file paths instead of iterating kModules, and app/test/module_costs_test.dart:28-33 walks only lib/ and web/, never test/ - so a sixth module is simply absent from the map and its stock goes unchecked, and even for the five only one file per module is scanned (lib/modules/*/thread_row.dart and lib/modules/dates/dates_module.dart are never read).
findings.why: Rule 3: the claim is that a new module is a directory plus one line, and this is a file outside every module's directory that a sixth module must be added to for its guarantee to keep holding - a guard that loses coverage silently rather than failing.

findings.where: the dispatch at lines 91-93 and _serveStatic at 304-329
findings.what: Any request whose path does not start with '/v1' is served from pwaRoot with no authentication check at all, falling back to index.html for anything not found; no test covers this branch.
findings.why: Rule 7 says the host refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key. The PWA has to be fetchable before a pairing exists, so the exemption is reasonable, but it is a whole unauthenticated surface on the tailnet that the rule does not carve out and nothing asserts the shape of.

findings.what: The rule that must fail the build names thirteen packages plus dart:indexed_db and dart:html, but not package:web or dart:js_interop, both of which reach window.localStorage and IndexedDB with no package dependency; app/lib/media/local_uri_web.dart:1 and :4 import both from outside lib/spine/ today.
findings.why: Rule 1 is the one rule the brief says fails the build, so a route past it matters even unexercised - that file currently only mints Blob object URLs (:12-14), but the next web-side file to reach for browser storage would not trip the guard.

findings.where: the case at lines 121-125 and the early return at line 83
findings.what: 'the pulse and the modules have something to say' asserts only that two regions build without throwing (via draw at :65-76, whose sole assertion is takeException() is null), while its two neighbours at :105 and :113 assert content; and :83 returns silently rather than calling markTestSkipped when the bundle has no seeded year, so that case reports as passing on an unseeded build.
findings.why: Rule 9: a name that promises the regions say something over a body that checks only that they do not crash, and one case that goes green when its precondition is absent instead of saying so.

findings.what: The comment reads 'and the eighteen the registry holds are all of them present' above a hand-written list of seventeen ids; passed_on is missing, and it is missing from the identical list at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:21-25 as well.
findings.why: Rule 2 asks for a test asserting the same list as the registry and the document; these two tests name the types by hand and neither names them all, so the shelf module's type is held only by the doc-table comparison.

what_is_working: The persistence boundary is real and the rule guarding it is hard to walk around: one package:sqlite3 import (spine/store/store_sqlite.dart:10) and one package:idb_shim import (spine/store/store_web.dart:4), both under lib/spine/store/, and I probed persistence_boundary_test's regex with thirteen shapes of directive - conditional, deferred, exported, double-quoted, broken over three lines - and it caught every one that names a driver.

Typing and presence cannot become events by accident rather than by convention: Spine.append routes through specOf (spine/spine.dart:219-221), which throws on any id not in kEventTypes, and the same check is applied to events off the wire (:274, :284), so 'typing' has no path into the log even if someone called append with it. transport_local_test.dart:287-302 asserts both logs stay at length zero after a typing and a presence frame have crossed.

Read markers and reactions are excluded upstream of drawing: projections/thread.dart:278-287 returns before _add, so no ThreadItem exists for a renderer to be asked about, and marginality is asked of the registry rather than of a fourth list (thread_types_test.dart:90-110).

The fifth module genuinely cost one line, and the proof reads source rather than trusting a comment: module_costs_test.dart:35-75 forbids every handle a shared file could key a per-module table off - the module id, each event type, and each renderer id - across lib/ and web/ both, which is what caught the service worker's old per-type table; web/push/sw.js:143-157 now reads its per-type words out of the store and keeps no knowledge of any type. I re-ran the grep by hand and found nothing outside the module directories and the spine registry.

The fifth module's own commit (ffc5821d) touched nothing under the first four modules' directories, and the shared files it did touch have since been dissolved: the thread body table is assembled from kModules (renderers.dart:179), the paper from Module.stocks (assignment.dart:34-41), the desk share from Module.share (us_region.dart:84-93), the search facets from the registry (search_page.dart:55-62).

There is no path in the Tailscale transport that reaches a wildcard bind: hostBind checks the address before it does anything else (tailscale_transport.dart:75), isTailnetAddress admits only the two real ranges (tailnet.dart:22-33), and with nothing on the tailnet the transport throws with a sentence a person can read rather than falling back to something that works.

742 of the 744 files under assets/ carry an entry naming one of ten generators, all ten of which exist on disk; the two that do not are index sidecars named with their reason in tools/check/manifest.py:21-23. No generator in tools/ or blender/ makes a network call, and the three fonts are built from a stroke-skeleton table rather than started from a downloaded face.

The suite runs clean and is unusually substantive for a suite of this size: 160 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. Several guards carry comments naming the exact bug they replaced and the reason the previous version of the guard could not fail - every_module_is_on_the_desk_test.dart:120-127 is the clearest, a test rewritten because the first version measured the harness's own Column.

My only use of git was three targeted queries: git rev-list --all for a content scan of history blobs, git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H per module directory to date each module's arrival, and git show --stat --format= on one commit hash to count the fifth module's diff by path. No commit message was read. A prior critic's report surfaced inside the output of the history content scan; I did not open the file and no claim here rests on it.
verdict: The architecture the brief asks for is really there and, unusually, it is held in place by guards that read source rather than by comments claiming it. There is one log with one boundary: two storage drivers, both under lib/spine/store/, and a rule I attacked with thirteen shapes of import directive and could not get past for any driver in the dependency set. Typing and presence cannot reach the log even by mistake, because append validates against the registry and neither is in it. A read marker never becomes a row object, so nothing downstream can draw one. The fifth module cost one line in registry.dart plus its own directory, the commit that added it touched nothing under the first four, and module_costs_test proves the property today by forbidding every module id, event type and renderer id from every file in lib/ and web/ outside the module's own directory - which is a stronger claim than the rule asks for and it passes. The host has no path to a wildcard bind; assets all name a generator that exists, and nothing was fetched. The suite runs clean: 160 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed. What holds this at the floor rather than above it is two leaks of exactly the kind row 04 is about. First, docs/EVENT_TYPES.md promises search 'by family' and 'by intensity' for the two feeling types and the code indexes neither, unseen because the only doc-versus-code test compares the type-id column and nothing else. Second, and worse because a person can see it, summaryOf hands the raw feeling_id to search results and to the composer's replying-to strip, so 390 of the seeded year's 1,340 feelings read as 'noor sent warm_palm' in one surface while the thread draws the same event as an object with its written name - the same event saying two different things depending on which way you came to it, which is the failure this codebase's own comments say the single-sentence rule exists to prevent. The guard against it exists and is defeated by its own fixture. Neither is architectural, both are seams, and the row meets its floor at 13; but a build whose central object reads as a database key in the one screen made for finding things has not finished making the log coherent, and the third finding - a per-module table in a test file that a sixth module would fall out of silently - is the same shape of problem arriving a year early.
